ownership_reason: Only the gold decides whether a non-null alternate of the union can appear in a numeric context: it judges each alternate by an object type, the alternate itself if it is an object type and otherwise the object type it is autoboxed to, through that object type's own matchesNumberContext. Hops 1, 3 and 4 pass the alternates along unchanged; hop 2 decides only the null type (null converts to zero) and documents that every other alternate is passed on unchanged and judged one by one. Once the gold gives the number alternate no object type, the union (number|undefined) matches a numeric context only if a caller decides a primitive itself or replaces the gold. The gold's javadoc promises whether a value of one of the types can appear in a numeric context; a number can, and the variant answers false for (number|undefined). The convention is pinned outside the gold: JSType.dereference ('Autoboxes the type') and JSType.findPropertyType (ObjectType.cast(autoboxesTo())) judge a primitive by the object type it is autoboxed to; NumberType.matchesNumberContext and PrototypeObjectType.matchesNumberContext (Number/Boolean/String object types) give the answers; JSTypeTest::testNumberValueType, ::testNumberObjectType, ::testStringValueType and ::testBooleanValueType assert them, and TypeCheckTest::testStringComparison2 passes through the chain (the null alternate counts).
